readme:
### What it does

Gives your AI agent structured access to Ubiquiti UniFi network controllers. Monitor device health, track connected clients, inspect firewall policies, review traffic routes, and manage WLANs — all through 18 focused MCP tools with token-efficient output.

Built on [aiounifi](https://github.com/Kane610/aiounifi) (MIT, powers the Home Assistant integration), which handles UniFi OS vs classic controller detection, cookie-based auth with CSRF tokens, and TOTP 2FA.

### How it differs from other UniFi MCPs

| | This plugin | sirkirby/unifi-mcp | enuno/unifi-mcp-server |
|---|---|---|---|
| Focus | Monitoring + security (18 tools) | Full management (161 tools) | Full management (74 tools) |
| Design for | LLM agents (token-efficient) | Claude Code (lazy loading) | General MCP clients |
| Multi-controller | Native (env var config) | Single controller | Multi-mode (local/cloud) |
| Write safety | Dual-gated (env + confirm) | Preview-then-confirm | Permission model |
| 2FA support | TOTP via aiounifi | TOTP support | API key option |
| Output | Pipe-delimited, compact | Full JSON | Full JSON |

Use this plugin for agent-driven monitoring and security visibility. Use sirkirby/unifi-mcp (available as community listing) when you need full network configuration management.

### Multi-instance support

Designed for multi-instance deployment. Each instance authenticates independently with its own controller credentials. Use cases:

- **Home + office** — separate UniFi controllers at different sites
- **Property portfolio** — different networks at different addresses
- **MSP** — manage multiple customer networks

Within a single instance, `UNIFI_CONTROLLERS=home,office` supports multiple controllers with independent sessions.

### Token efficiency

The UniFi API returns verbose JSON with deeply nested objects. This plugin reformats everything into compact, pipe-delimited output:

- Device listing: ~50 tokens per device (vs ~800 raw)
- Client listing: ~40 tokens per client with signal, experience, blocked status
- Firewall policies: ~30 tokens per policy

### Safety model

Read tools work immediately — devices, clients, firewall, traffic routes, DPI, port forwards.

Write operations require `UNIFI_WRITE_ENABLED=true` (environment variable, set in plugin config). Destructive operations additionally require `confirm=true` per-call:

| Operation | Gate |
|-----------|------|
| Block client | write + confirm |
| Unblock client | write |
| Reconnect client | write |
| Toggle WLAN | write |
| Toggle traffic route | write |
| Restart device | write + confirm |

### Authentication

Two auth modes map to two endpoint families. Provide at least one; provide both for full tool coverage.

| Mode | Credential | Endpoint family | Tools reached | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **API key** (recommended) | `UNIFI_API_KEY` | Integration API (`/proxy/network/integration/v1/…`) | Network/VLAN tools (`unifi_networks`, `unifi_network`, VLAN create) | Official, Ubiquiti-supported, stateless. Generate at Control Plane → Settings → Admins → API Key. |
| **Session** | `UNIFI_USERNAME` + `UNIFI_PASSWORD` | Legacy controller API (`/api/s/…`) via aiounifi | Monitoring tools (devices, clients, WLANs, firewall, traffic rules/routes, port forwards, DPI, info, sites) | Unofficial private API. Local admin account only — **not** a UI.com SSO login. Cookie/CSRF session; TOTP 2FA via `UNIFI_TOTP_SECRET` (base32). |

**API-key-only** is the simplest config and covers network configuration. Add username+password to also reach the monitoring tools — calling a session-only tool with just an API key returns a clear capability-gap error, not a crash. Supports both UniFi OS (port 443) and classic controllers (port 8443); SSL verification configurable (disabled by default for self-signed certs common on UDM hardware).

The tool reference below lists the session-auth monitoring tools. The network/VLAN tools reached by API-key mode are documented in the [repository README](https://github.com/groupthink-dev/ubiquiti-unifi-blade-mcp).

### Tool reference

| Tool | Type | What it does |
|------|------|--------------|
| unifi_info | read | Health check — controller version, hostname, device/client counts, write gate |
| unifi_sites | read | List sites on the controller |
| unifi_devices | read | APs, switches, gateways — model, state, clients, uptime, firmware |
| unifi_device | read | Full detail — port table with PoE, firmware, upgrade status |
| unifi_clients | read | Connected clients — name, IP, SSID, signal, experience, blocked |
| unifi_client | read | Full detail — TX/RX, vendor (OUI), AP association |
| unifi_wlans | read | WLANs — name, enabled/disabled, security, guest flag |
| unifi_firewall | read | Firewall policies — name, action, enabled/disabled |
| unifi_traffic_routes | read | Traffic routes — description, enabled/disabled, target |
| unifi_traffic_rules | read | Traffic rules — description, action, enabled/disabled |
| unifi_port_forwards | read | Port forwards — name, protocol, external → internal |
| unifi_dpi | read | DPI restriction groups and apps |
| unifi_block_client | gated | Block a client from the network (write + confirm) |
| unifi_unblock_client | gated | Unblock a previously blocked client |
| unifi_reconnect_client | gated | Force a wireless client to reconnect |
| unifi_toggle_wlan | gated | Enable or disable an SSID |
| unifi_toggle_traffic_route | gated | Enable or disable a traffic route |
| unifi_restart_device | gated | Restart an AP, switch, or gateway (write + confirm) |

env.name: UNIFI_API_KEY
env.description: Integration API key (Control Plane → Settings → Admins → API Key). Drives the official stateless Integration API — network/VLAN tools. Use INSTEAD OF username+password, or alongside for full tool coverage.

env.name: UNIFI_USERNAME
env.description: Controller admin username (session auth). Drives the legacy /api/s/ controller API — monitoring tools (devices, clients, firewall, WLANs). Pair with UNIFI_PASSWORD.

env.name: UNIFI_PASSWORD
env.description: Controller admin password (session auth — pairs with UNIFI_USERNAME)

env.name: UNIFI_PORT
env.description: Controller port (443 for UniFi OS, 8443 for classic)

setup.blurb: Monitor your UniFi network — device health, connected clients, firewall policies, traffic routes, and DPI restrictions. Multi-controller support for home and office.
setup.help_text:
Two authentication modes — provide at least one (both for full tool coverage):

• API key (recommended): an Integration API key from Control Plane → Settings → Admins → API Key. Drives the official, Ubiquiti-supported Integration API — the network/VLAN tools (unifi_networks, unifi_network). Stateless, no session.

• Username + password: a LOCAL controller admin account (not a UI.com SSO login). Drives the legacy session API — the monitoring tools (devices, clients, firewall, WLANs, traffic rules/routes, port forwards, DPI, info). Add the TOTP secret if the account has 2FA.

API-key-only is the simplest setup and covers network configuration; add username+password to also reach the monitoring tools.

fields.label: Controller Host
fields.help: IP or hostname of the UniFi controller (UDM, UDM-Pro, Cloud Key, or self-hosted Network app).

fields.label: API Key
fields.help: Integration API key (Control Plane → Settings → Admins → API Key). Unlocks the network/VLAN tools via the official stateless Integration API. Recommended — use alone, or alongside username+password for full coverage.

fields.label: Username (session auth)
fields.help: Local controller account username — not a UI.com SSO account. Required for the monitoring tools (devices, clients, firewall, WLANs). Pair with Password.

fields.label: Password (session auth)
fields.help: Password for the local controller account. Required (with Username) for the monitoring tools.

fields.label: TOTP secret (2FA, optional)
fields.help: Base32-encoded TOTP secret — only if the session-auth account has 2FA enabled.

fields.label: Verify SSL
fields.help: Disable for self-signed certificates (common on UDM hardware)

fields.label: Enable write operations
fields.help: Allow client blocking, WLAN toggling, and device restarts

scenarios.label: Network security audit
scenarios.body: Run unifi_info for controller health, then unifi_devices to check all devices are connected and firmware is current. List unifi_clients and flag any unknown or blocked devices. Review unifi_firewall for policy gaps and unifi_port_forwards for exposed services.

scenarios.label: Client investigation
scenarios.body: Call unifi_clients to list all connected clients. For suspicious entries, use unifi_client with the MAC address for full detail (vendor, signal, TX/RX, AP). If rogue, use unifi_block_client with confirm=true to isolate the device.

scenarios.label: Morning network health check
scenarios.body: Run unifi_info to verify all controllers are connected. Check unifi_devices for any disconnected APs or switches and firmware upgrades available. Review unifi_clients for unexpected device count changes. Check unifi_traffic_routes and unifi_dpi for any disabled restrictions.
